neighbours.label: the subject/auxiliary of a clause saying a disease will be detected by a medical test ('the chance that it will be found')
fire: If a lump is present, a mammogram raises the odds that it will be found in time.
Should the cancer return, the yearly scan means it will probably be detected quickly.
If there is a polyp, a colonoscopy makes it likely that it will be spotted and removed.
When a tumour is small, an MRI increases the chance that it will be seen at all.
If the infection has spread, a blood culture makes it more likely that it will show up.
Where a fracture exists, a CT scan improves the chance that it will be picked up early.
If any disease is lurking, routine screening means it will usually be caught at stage one.
If a clot has formed, an ultrasound makes it far more likely that it will be identified.
quiet: If you exercise often, a healthy diet raises the odds that you will live longer.
Should the pain return, the clinic recommends rest and a warm compress at home.
If there is a queue, the receptionist makes sure everyone gets a numbered ticket.
When a patient is small, the nurse uses a child-sized cuff for the blood pressure.
If the weather is fine, the hospital garden is open to visitors in the afternoon.
Where a ward is busy, extra staff are brought in from the neighbouring hospital.
If any forms are missing, the office will post them to your home address.
If a bed is free, the patient can stay overnight and go home in the morning.

notes: Card: broad (1.5%), peaks on ' test', ' diagnostic', ' will' in cancer-detection text. Probe: only 'a bone scan makes it more likely that it will be found early' fired strongly (0.71, peak ' it'); 'blood test is a check of how well...' 0.30; ' diagnostic' 0.17; 'test of patience', screening/'caught', interviews all <0.10. So the test targets the narrow detection frame 'test -> it will be found'. Near misses keep the hospital setting and the conditional frame but drop detection.
